significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that a rise in task-feature disentanglement reliably precedes or coincides with capability onset and predicts that onset more smoothly than loss, plus the form-(ii) mechanistic conclusion that "ablating the newly disentangled features selectively removes the emergent skill while sparing others." This would establish both a behavioral regularity and a causal geometric mechanism, constraining when other capabilities should emerge and distinguishing internal reorganization from the metric-only account discussed by Schaeffer et al. (2023); it is therefore more consequential than merely finding a decodable capability feature. Verified-false and verified-true are distinguishable, although "better and more smoothly" lacks a quantitative bound: failure of both the cross-checkpoint coupling and selective causal effect would rule out disentanglement as a general explanation rather than merely fail to locate one feature. In the topic-substitution check, the generic language–intelligence topic would not support this score; the score comes from the claim-specific temporal coupling and causal account.

reach.justification: The named handle is the checkpoint-level "feature separability" transition, proposed as an "early-warning signal for capability onset" rather than only a post-hoc explanation; however, the wording "precedes or coincides" means usable lead time is asserted only in part of the hypothesis. After feature extraction is recalibrated on another model, the claimed relation still predicts that increasing separability should forecast a behavioral transition, so more than a model-specific direction survives, with prospective users including researchers and practitioners monitoring training for new capabilities. The hypothesis speaks generically about "so-called emergent abilities" and multiple capabilities rather than one task, but it does not state robust invariance across architectures, training recipes, or modalities, limiting how confidently the handle travels. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the transferable predictor and monitoring handle, not the broad importance of language and intelligence, provide the above-median reach.
